text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on October 16 in history. 1430 - James II born. Known as "James of the fiery face" he was King of Scotland from 1437 to 1460. 1555 - Oxford martyrs and English Protestant Reformers Hugh Latimer and Nicholas Ridley were burned at the stake after being found guilty of heresy.
1758 - Noah Webster born. U.S. lexicographer who in 1828 published the dictionary which now bears his name.
1793 - Marie Antoinette, Queen of France and wife of King Louis XVI, was guillotined for treason.
1813 - The Battle of Leipzig began. In the three-day battle the allied armies won a decisive victory against the French.
1846 - For the first time, a major operation was carried out using ether as an anaesthetic. Dr John Warren performed the removal of a tumour at Massachusetts General Hospital, Boston.
1854 - Oscar Wilde (Fingal O'Flahertie Wills), Irish playwright, poet, novelist, and renowned wit born.
1859 - U.S. anti-slavery activist John Brown led a raid on Harper's Ferry, Virginia and seized the armoury to provide for his militia. Brown was captured and later hanged.

1863 - British statesman Sir (Joseph) Austen Chamberlain born. He was foreign secretary 1924-1929 and a member of Lloyd George's war cabinet. He was a joint winner of the Nobel Peace Prize in 1925 for negotiating the Locarno Pact.
1886 - David Ben-Gurion (David Green) born. He became first prime minister of Israel from 1948 and again in 1957.
1888 - Eugene (Gladstone) O'Neill born. U.S. playwright, he became the first U.S. dramatist to win the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1936. Best known for his "Long Day's Journey into Night".

1890 - Michael Collins born. Irish politician and revolutionary leader. He signed the treaty which led to the Irish Free State in December 1921 and became its chairman. He was shot dead in an ambush by extremists on August 22 1922.
1916 - The first birth control clinic in the United States was opened by Margaret Sanger in Brooklyn, New York.
1927 - Guenter Grass born. Leading German writer he also became a speech writer for Willy Brandt. His reputation grew enormously with the publication (1959) of "The Tin Drum".
1945 - The Food and Agricultural Organisation (FAO) of the United Nations was established, with the main aims of raising levels of nutrition and improving standards of living.
1946 - Top Nazi war criminals were hanged at Nuremburg. Among them were foreign minister Joachim von Ribbentrop and Field Marshal Wilhelm Keitel.
1951 - Liaquat Ali Khan, Prime Minister of Pakistan, was shot dead while addressing a public meeting in Rawalpindi.
1963 - Ludwig Erhard was elected Chancellor of West Germany in succession to Konrad Adenauer.
1964 - China exploded its first nuclear bomb at the Lop Nor test site in Sinkiang.
1973 - U.S. jazz drummer and band leader Gene Krupa died aged 64.
1978 - Cardinal Karol Wojtyla of Poland was elected Pope and took the name John Paul II, the first non-Italian Pope for 456 years.
1981 - Israeli general and Minister of Defence Moshe Dayan died of a heart attack. He became a hero in Israel with his successful completion of the "Six-Day War" in 1967.
1989 - Cornel Wilde died. U.S. actor of stage and screen he was also remembered for his ecological views. He was especially notable in "A Song to Remember" and "Naked Prey". He was 74.
1995 - In a huge demonstration near the U.S. Capitol, Nation of Islam leader Louis Farrakhan, offered a thunderous sermon portraying America as a white supremacist society.
